title: Decretum Gratiani (manuscrito iluminado, BnF)
description: Manuscrito iluminado do Decretum Gratiani (Concordia discordantium canonum, c. 1140), coletânea de direito canônico compilada pelo monge Graciano em Bolonha, conservado na Bibliothèque nationale de France. Os manuscritos do Decretum são célebres por suas miniaturas iluminadas — especialmente capitais historiadas e frontispícios — que representam a Justitia como figura feminina com espada e balança, cenas de julgamento e disputas jurídicas. Produzido nos scriptoria bolonheses no século XIII, o exemplar da BnF integra a tradição dos manuscritos jurídicos iluminados que constituem o principal corpus medieval da iconografia da justiça. Digitalizado e disponível na plataforma Gallica.

title: Illustrations de Calendrier et compost des bergiers (Da
description: Illustrations from the 'Calendar and Almanac of Shepherds' featuring the dance of death and allegorical figures including Justice. An early representation of Justice as a female figure within the memento mori tradition — the intersection of death, morality, and law.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte-rendu au Roi pa
description: Engraved allegorical frontispiece designed for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781), the public financial report that became a landmark in Ancien Régime transparency. Female allegorical figures — variously interpreted as Justice, Abundance, and Truth — frame the royal accounting. An early instance of female allegory deployed in the visual rhetoric of fiscal governance.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte rendu au Roi pa
description: Second variant of the allegorical engraving designed as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). Female allegorical figures in a variant compositional arrangement. Documents the multiple print versions in circulation around this seminal text on royal finances and public accountability.

title: Allégorie pour servir de frontispice au compte-rendu au
description: Third allegorical engraving serving as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). This variant reinforces the corpus of female allegorical imagery mobilized around the question of royal fiscal accountability in the late Ancien Régime. The three Necker frontispieces (FR-015, FR-016, FR-017) together document the visual politics of the transparency debate.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen
description: Engraved broadside of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789), designed by Le Barbier l'aîné and engraved by Laurent and Dien. The composition frames the text of the Declaration with two female allegorical figures — Liberty with Phrygian cap and Justice with scales — flanking a radiating triangle (Eye of Providence). Canonical image of Revolutionary visual rhetoric fusing law, allegory, and print.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (varian
description: Anonymous engraved broadside variant of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789). Presents the text of the Declaration within an allegorical decorative framework featuring female figures. Variant edition circulating alongside the canonical Le Barbier design, reflecting the proliferation of allegorical print culture during the Revolution.

title: [Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité — portrait allégorique d'
description: Revolutionary allegorical print combining the motto Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité with a portrait of Ernouf. Designed by Garneray and engraved by Quéverdo, this composite image exemplifies the visual culture of the Directory period, deploying female allegorical figures to embody Republican values alongside the honored portrait. Documents the consolidation of Marianne iconography in post-Terror Republican print culture.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple (Eugène Delacroix)
description: 'Liberty Leading the People' — the iconic image of the July Revolution of 1830. A bare-breasted female figure (Liberty/Marianne) leads armed citizens over barricades, holding the tricolour flag and a musket. The most powerful visual crystallization of the republic-as-woman — Warner's central case study, Agulhon's key image. Foundational for the entire Iconocracy project.

title: Liberty Leading the People
L'envoyé de la Justice
pre_iconographic: Central MALE winged figure in cruciform pose, nearly nude. Sword and torch. In upper right, luminous FEMALE figure in classical drapery holding torch, 'JUSTICE' inscribed in sky. Fallen figures below. Deep chiaroscuro.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: DELEGATION: Justice (female, background) sends male angel as armed envoy
iconographic.tradicao: Christian angelology meets republican allegory; Miltonian/Romantic

ico_funcao: Female principle generates but does not execute justice. State violence by male body authorized by female source
description: Engraving titled 'The Envoy of Justice' — depicting a figure sent by Justice (as a female allegorical power). Early example in the series of Justice representations by Chifflart.

title: Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants (naïades e
pre_iconographic: Cyanotype of TWO engravings. LEFT: Nude female with children (naiads), pastoral. RIGHT: Marianne in white robe, radiant crown, olive branch, teaching children before tablet 'LIBERTÉ ÉGALITÉ FRATERNITÉ / CATÉCHISME RÉPUBLICAIN'.

iconographic.tradicao: Third Republic civic imagery; Ferry-era school decoration

ico_funcao: Civic education through maternal-allegorical body. Quasi-religious CATÉCHISME structure
description: Engravings depicting naiads and Marianne teaching the alphabet to children. Powerful image of the Republic-as-woman as educator — embodying the republican ideal of laïcité and public instruction through a female allegorical figure.

title: La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité
pre_iconographic: Three female figures in dynamic aerial flight swooping toward 3-4 grotesque male figures cowering on rocky ground. Classical robes billowing. Lead female extends arm in accusatory pursuit. Mountainous landscape. Etching, monochrome, signed 'F. Chifflart'.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: Triad: Justice, Vengeance, Truth in punitive pursuit

ico_funcao: Legitimation of punitive justice through divine feminine agency
description: Engraving depicting three female allegorical figures: Justice, Vengeance, and Truth. A powerful composition showing Justice as a dominant female presence, flanked by Truth and divine Vengeance — key triad in French republican allegorical vocabulary.

title: Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité
pre_iconographic: Female figure atop cubic pedestal, semi-nude with classical drapery, holding scales. Wing/billowing drapery behind. 4-5 nude male caryatids supporting pedestal. Crowd at base. Rocky promontory. Signed 'F. Chifflart'.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: Justice triumphant, elevated to monument; Truth implied by nudity

ico_funcao: Architectonic legitimation — Justice as capstone of social order supported by male labor
description: Engraving showing the triumph of Justice and Truth as female allegorical figures. Complete state with full lettering. Part of Chifflart's series on juridical allegory.

title: Le hochet de la République (Jean Veber)
pre_iconographic: Satirical print by Jean Veber depicting the Republic as/with a hochet (baby rattle). Caricatural style, likely exaggerated features. Monochrome engraving/lithograph. From Le Rire or L'Assiette au beurre tradition.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: La République reduced to toy — infantilization of republican symbolism
iconographic.tradicao: Third Republic satirical press (Le Rire, L'Assiette au beurre); Daumier, Gill, Rops lineage

ico_funcao: Delegitimation through infantilization — republican allegory as empty signifier, a rattle shaken to pacify
description: Satirical print 'The Rattle of the Republic' by Jean Veber. The Republic as a woman reduced to a toy or rattle — a critical/ironic commentary on the infantilization or trivialization of republican symbolism through its female form.

title: 5 Francs Hercule — La République et La Justice flanquan
description: Hercules standing center flanked by two female allegories: Republic (left, with pike topped by Phrygian cap) and Justice/Equality (right, with triangular level). Design by Dupré (1795), reissued 1848 and 1870. Banned during Second Empire for republican symbols.

title: La République aimable (Félicien Rops)
pre_iconographic: Standing female, hand on hip. Fitted dress with ruffled collar, visible decollete. Diminished Phrygian cap. Shield inscribed 'RES PUBLICA / THIERS / ETAT!'. Ironic smirk. Lorgnette. Drypoint etching. 'Respublica Amabilis. 1871'.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: SATIRICAL Marianne — Rops grotesques the Republic as 'aimable' (ironic)
iconographic.tradicao: Belgian/French satirical print; Rops transgressive eroticization
iconographic.pathosformel: Standing/confronting — Provokation formula; lorgnette reverses male gaze

ico_funcao: Delegitimation — satirical critique. Allegory used AGAINST the state
description: Satirical engraving by Belgian-French artist Félicien Rops depicting 'The Amiable Republic' — a subversive or eroticized representation of the Republic as a woman. Critical for understanding the contested gendered nature of republican allegory and its use in satirical press.

title: Piastre de Commerce — Marianne Assise avec Fasces
description: Marianne seated left on throne holding fasces, wearing radiate crown. Wheat bundles to left, anchor to right. Reverse: INDO-CHINE FRANÇAISE. Colonial trade coin for Indochina.

title: The French Crisis: Madame La République
pre_iconographic: Political cartoon of 'Madame La République' during a moment of crisis (1887 Boulangist crisis). Caricatural style of Third Republic press. Monochrome engraving. Phrygian cap probable. Textual caption integrated.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: Marianne in crisis — Republic under political stress during Boulangist challenge
iconographic.tradicao: Third Republic political press caricature (Daumier, Gill, Cham tradition)

ico_funcao: Dramatizes institutional fragility through the feminized body politic
description: Political cartoon from 1887 showing 'Madame La République' during the French political crisis. The Republic personified as a woman under stress — a key document of how female allegory was deployed during political instability.

title: Semeuse 1 Franc silver coin (Oscar Roty)
Semeuse — Selo Definitivo da República Francesa (Oscar
description: Marianne in flowing robes and Phrygian cap sowing seeds with extended right arm, seed bag under left arm. Rising sun on horizon (1903 version). Design from Roty medal (1887), adapted for coin (1897) then stamp (1903). Quintessential NORMATIVE Marianne: peaceful, productive, nurturing.

title: [Notre-Dame des colonies] : [estampe] / Jean Veber
La République nous appelle... (Steinlen)
pre_iconographic: WWI recruitment poster (1915, Steinlen). Dynamic Marianne in Phrygian cap and classical drapery, striding/summoning. Social-realist lithographic style with earth tones and muted reds. 'La République nous appelle...' Soldiers responding below.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: Republic-as-mother calling children to defend the patrie
iconographic.tradicao: Steinlen's social-realist poster tradition; WWI propaganda
iconographic.pathosformel: Summoning/commanding — active mobilizing Marianne, more corporeal than Lelong's

description: WWI recruitment poster: 'The Republic calls us...' — Marianne as a summoning female figure, calling citizens to arms. Steinlen's powerful composition shows the Republic-as-woman as a quasi-maternal/military figure demanding sacrifice.

title: Journée du Poilu, 25 et 26 décembre 1915, organisée par
description: WWI charity poster by Steinlen (1915) for the 'Journée du Poilu' (Soldier's Day, December 25–26), organized by the French Parliament to raise funds for soldiers at the front. The composition depicts a French soldier in the foreground, with a female figure — embodying the Republic/Marianne — in an embrace or gesture of support behind him. One of Steinlen's key contributions to French WWI visual culture, combining social realism with Republican allegorical tradition.

title: Bons de la Défense nationale.
En avant Armée de l'Epargne, C'est pour la Patrie.
République Française: 3e Emprunt de la Défense national
pre_iconographic: WWI war bond poster (1917, René Lelong). Monumental Marianne in Phrygian cap and tricolor drapery, arm raised, towering above marching poilus. Vertical composition, polychrome lithograph. 'RÉPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE / 3e EMPRUNT DE LA DÉFENSE NATIONALE'.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: War-Marianne — mobilizing Republic summoning citizens to financial sacrifice

ico_funcao: State deploys feminized image to command masculine sacrifice. The poster IS a state financial instrument (war bond).
description: WWI propaganda poster for the 3rd National Defense loan. Marianne stands triumphantly above soldiers, embodying the Republic rallying her citizens to war. The female allegory mobilized for military propaganda — a critical junction of gender, state power, and visual persuasion.

Buste de la République (Agence Rol)
pre_iconographic: Press photograph (Agence Rol, early 20th c.) of a sculpted Marianne bust: female from chest up on socle, classical drapery at shoulders, Phrygian cap, idealized generic features. Isolated against neutral background. Monochromatic silver gelatin print. Bust terminates body at chest.

iconographic.motivo_alegorico: La République / Marianne — canonical bust form for 36,000+ mairies
iconographic.tradicao: Third Republic civic bust typology (Doriot, Injalbert, Lagriffoul ateliers)
iconographic.pathosformel: None — total hieratic immobility. The bust format eliminates all gesture.

ico_funcao: The bust IS the state. Mandated by circular for every commune. The largest serial deployment of a female allegorical form in modern European history.
description: Press photograph of a bust sculpture representing the French Republic. Busts of Marianne became ubiquitous in French town halls (mairies) under the Third Republic — the multiplication of the female allegorical form across thousands of civic spaces.
